title: Choose the Signal Interlocking composition
question: The Signal Interlocking direction is approved. Which composition makes the PortWatch listener and its owner easiest to inspect? Choose one; every example is illustrative.

options.label: Interlocking field
options.lineage: railway signal cabin plans and interlocking diagrams
options.thesis: Every listener reads as an occupied route with a traceable owner.
options.viewport: A narrow port selector leads into a broad Port → Process → Project field; a compact inspector holds command, path, and the confirmed termination action.
options.risk: Several route colors can imply states the scanner does not measure; keep status literal and uniform.

options.label: Route field
options.thesis: Trace each listener horizontally through its process to the detected project.
options.viewport: A slim scan and filter strip sits above a compact port list, wide horizontal route diagram, and right-hand inspector.
options.risk: The route must describe only the observed port-to-process and detected-project relationship.

options.label: Signal ledger
options.thesis: A clean listener ledger leads into one compact route for the selected port.
options.viewport: A wide, readable port table sits beside an inspector; one compact trace shows the selected port, process, and project.
options.risk: Avoid encoding availability or process health through signal color; all rows are listening TCP records.
